segments: 546 Chronography of Barhebraeus.
Ayas,
and they burned it and plundered it.
However, they found none of its inhabitants in it,
since all of them had fled by sea
and entered the new fortress
which they had built in the midst of the sea.
And when they had plundered whatever fell into their hands,
they departed.
And again others entered, a third time.
Then others gathered, a fourth time,
and they invaded the country in the week of the Fast of Nineveh, of that year ninety-three [693 AH = 1294 AD]:
and they reached as far as Tell Hamdun,
and took much spoil.
And as they were leaving,
the Armenians seized the passes against them,
and put them all to the edge of the sword,
and stripped off their armor,
and flayed the skins of their heads.
And they loaded {OCR?} horses with loads of armor, and lances, and swords, and scalps with their hair,
and sent them to the King of Kings.
And after a few days,
the governor of the fortress of Bira,
whose name was Haydar,
gathered a force of about two thousand horsemen,
and attacked the fortress of Zaid.
And many of the Christians fled and took refuge in the great mosque of the Arabs and were saved;
while others defended themselves in a place called "Upon the Pillar",
and the raiders were not able to come against them,
because that place is rugged, like a ravine.
Then those accursed men, having captured about four thousand women and children,
crossed the Euphrates over against Melitene,
and plundered its territory.
And they found in the village of 'Arqa a great multitude of Christians,
and them also they carried off into captivity,
and went to Syria.
Now Mengu Timur, when he returned from Syria,
came to Abaqa at Baghdad, grieved and mourning over the defeat that had happened to him;
and he took it upon himself to return again to Syria.
And when he returned and reached the island of Qardu (Jazirat Ibn Umar),
a certain informer,
whose name was Safi Qarqubi,
slandered the notables {OCR?} of the Island.
And because of this,
that Mengu Timur inflicted many evils upon them.
And they harbored resentment against him.
And one day, when he came out of the bath,
they found an opportunity and conspired with one of the cupbearers, and he gave him poison to drink.
And when his body was racked with pain,
he set out from the Island toward Nisibis.
